'''''Archontophoenix alexandrae''''', commonly known as '''Alexandra palm''', '''king palm''', '''northern Bangalow palm''', or '''feather palm''',{{R|RFK8|PASCOA|CRC}} is a palm endemic to [[Queensland]], Australia. It was named in honour of [[Alexandra of Denmark|Princess Alexandra]] of Denmark,{{R|COOPER2}} but is often erroneously referred to by the [[misnomer]] '''Alexander palm'''.

==Description==
''Archontophoenix alexandrae'' is a tall, solitary palm growing to a height of {{convert|30|m|ft|abbr=on}} with a trunk up to {{convert|30|cm|in|abbr=on}} diameter, often swollen at the base, and bearing prominent leaf scars.{{R|RFK8|PASCOA}} The graceful crown has 8 to 10 [[pinnate]], feather-like fronds that measure up to {{convert|4.5|m|ft|abbr=on}} in length, with 60 to 80 leaflets on each side of the midrib.{{R|RFK8|COOPER2}} The pinnae are dark green above and silvery-grey underneath, measuring up to {{convert|75|cm|in|abbr=on}} long, and the entire frond is usually twisted laterally.{{R|RFK8|PASCOA}} At the base of each frond is a large [[crownshaft]] up to {{convert|1|m|ft|abbr=on}} high, coloured light green.{{R|RFK8}}

===Flowers===

The [[inflorescence]] of ''Archontophoenix alexandrae'' is a [[panicle]], creamy white when first released from the protective sheath, or [[Bract#Spathe|prophyll]], that it develops within, and transitioning through light green as the fruits develop and finally to brown when it is shed from the tree. It measures between {{convert|50|and|100|cm|in|abbr=on}} wide by {{convert|50|cm|in|abbr=on}} long, and arises from the base of the crownshaft.{{R|RFK8|PASCOA|COOPER2}} Flowering occurs randomly throughout the year,{{R|COOPER2}} and it is not uncommon to find a group of these palms, some of which carry fruit and/or flowers while others carry neither. Individual flowers are 3-petalled, creamy-white in colour and quite small—the [[staminate]] (functionally male) flowers measuring up to {{convert|10|mm|in|abbr=on|1}} wide and the [[pistillate]] (functionally female) flowers up to {{convert|4|mm|in|abbr=on}}.{{R|RFK8}}

===Fruit===
The fruits are [[Glossary of botanical terms#ovoid|ovoid]] to [[Glossary of botanical terms#globose|globose]] with a persistent [[Glossary of botanical terms#calyx|calyx]]. They are initially green turning bright red when ripe. They measure around {{convert|10|-|14|mm|in|abbr=on|1}} in diameter and contain a single seed about {{convert|8|mm|in|abbr=on|1}} diameter.{{R|RFK8|COOPER2}}

==Taxonomy==
The species was originally described as ''Ptychosperma alexandrae'' by [[Ferdinand von Mueller]] in his eleven-volume work ''[[Fragmenta phytographiae Australiae]]'' in 1865.{{R|POWO1}} In 1875 the German botanists [[Hermann Wendland]] and Oscar Drude published a treatment of Australian palms in the journal ''Linnaea'' titled ''Palmae Australasicae'', in which this species was renamed ''Archontophoenix alexandrae''.{{R|POWO2}}

===Etymology===
The genus name is derived from the Ancient Greek [[wikt:ἄρχων|ἄρχων]] ({{Lang|grc-Latn|árkhōn}}), meaning 'chieftain' or 'ruler', combined with the palm genus [[Phoenix (plant)|''Phoenix'']], and refers to the regal stature of the trees. The [[Botanical name#Binary name|species epithet]] is given in honour of [[Alexandra of Denmark|Princess Alexandra]] of Denmark.{{R|COOPER2|PALMWEB}}

==Distribution and habitat==
[[File:Archontophoenix-alexandrae-SF20320.jpg|thumb|right|Alexandra palms dominate the forest in the flood zone beside Freshwater Creek, Cairns, Queensland.]]

The native range of this species is north-east and central-east [[Queensland]], from the [[Cape Melville|Melville Range]] in [[Cape York Peninsula]] to south of [[Gladstone, Queensland|Gladstone]].{{R|PASCOA|COOPER2}} The altitudinal range is from sea level to {{cvt|1000|m}}, although it is most commonly found in lowland [[Riparian zone|riparian]] rainforest alongside river courses and swamps, often in locations that are severely inundated during heavy rain events.{{R|RFK8|COOPER2}} Their ability to withstand these conditions allows them to become the dominant species.

==Ecology==
The fruit of the Alexandra palm is eaten by many bird species,{{R|COOPER2}} notably the [[metallic starling]] (''Aplonis metallica''), which often descend on a tree as a flock and may consume all of the ripe fruits within an hour. Other common bird species include the [[Torresian imperial pigeon]] (''Ducula spilorrhoa'') and the [[wompoo fruit dove]] (''Ptilinopus magnificus''). Fruits are also eaten by [[fruit bat]]s and the [[musky rat-kangaroo]] (''Hypsiprymnodon moschatus'').{{R|COOPER2}}

==Uses==
The [[Kuku Yalanji]] people of Far North Queensland ate the [[Heart of palm|palm heart]] of this species.{{R|AGTARPU}}

==Cultivation==
This species is easily grown from fresh seed, and is very popular in cultivation in Australia, both for private gardens and as a street and park tree.{{R|RFK8|JONES}} It is fast growing and will tolerate cooler climates outside the tropics where there are no frosts, and has been widely planted in many countries. It has become naturalised in Hawaii.{{R|HEAR}}
